meta.purpose: Golden questions for the retrieval-only evaluation (scripts/evaluate.py). Expected ids come from data/clusters.json and from the ticket text, never from a search result.
meta.dataset: data/tickets.json, 800 synthetic tickets, seed 42, as of 2026-10-25
notes: expected is a lower bound: the dataset can hold other tickets that also fit a question but are not labelled.
known_weak questions are reported on their own rows and are not part of the headline numbers.

type 'extra (assistant-drafted, not blind)' (ids A01 to A05): the questions were drafted by the assistant and adopted unchanged by the repository owner; the expected ids were drafted by the assistant from ticket text and generator metadata after reading the data, so they are not blind. A question the repository owner writes later is a new entry with author 'repository owner'.

questions.question: What happened in ticket OPS-1001?
questions.rationale: Plain ticket-id lookup; the exact-id path of app/rag.py must return it. Vector search alone ranks ids poorly.

questions.question: Which ticket is about purchase order PO-165700?
questions.rationale: PO number lookup. The validator checks that no other ticket contains PO-165700.

questions.question: Find the ticket for invoice INV-323839.
questions.rationale: Invoice number lookup. The validator checks that no other ticket contains INV-323839.

questions.question: What is the status of ticket OPS-9999?
questions.source: OPS-9999 does not exist (ids run OPS-1001 to OPS-1800)
questions.rationale: A missing id must produce no ticket and a missing reference, not a near neighbour.

questions.question: What caused the recurring VPN outages and how were they fixed?
questions.rationale: The project's standard demo question, so it was also used in manual tests (not independent of earlier work). Six tickets: three Infrastructure and three Customer Escalation about the same firmware crash loop.

questions.question: Why did dispatch stop at Chennai when the power went out?
questions.rationale: Facilities power-failure tickets and Logistics dispatch tickets share one root cause (generator never took the load).

questions.question: Why does the Bengaluru server room keep losing its cooling?
questions.rationale: Five tickets, one is worded 'HVAC failure' instead of 'cooling down', which tests a vocabulary variant inside a cluster.

questions.question: Which supplier started charging us more than the agreed rates without telling us?
questions.rationale: Vendor name is not in the question; the tickets say 'invoicing above agreed rates' and 'unannounced price increase'. Unlabelled competitors: CL-24 (RoadRunner Express fuel surcharge not in the contract) and OPS-1020 / OPS-1025 (SwiftHaul overcharge). A miss that retrieves those is not necessarily a retrieval failure.

questions.question: Why could customers not sign in to the portal at the same time?
questions.rationale: Federated login failure after the SSO certificate expired. The question says 'sign in', the cluster mixes 'single sign-on' and 'cannot sign in'.

questions.question: Why do we keep seeing rodents in the Chennai warehouse?
questions.rationale: Question says 'rodents'; one ticket says 'rodent sightings', another 'pest activity'.

questions.question: Why did TLS handshakes fail on the tracking service?
questions.rationale: Certificate-expiry tickets; the question uses 'TLS handshakes', the tickets say 'certificate expiry' and 'handshake failures'.

questions.question: Why did the bank refuse our vendor payment batch?
questions.rationale: Three Billing & Finance tickets about a payment file rejected with E2209. Unlabelled competitor: CL-28 (Orion Cold Systems payment run, also E2209), so some retrieved tickets may be relevant but not labelled.

questions.question: Why do we keep running out of stock before the replenishment order arrives?
questions.rationale: The labelled set is the six SKU-23104 tickets (reorder point too low / replenishment too late), CL-02. The question names no SKU and no cause. Other stockouts exist unlabelled: a text search finds 16 other Inventory tickets that mention a stockout, out of stock, reorder point or replenishment (8 with the same reorder-point story for other SKUs: OPS-1051, 1405, 1419, 1437, 1648, 1664, 1712, 1732; 8 backorder stockouts: OPS-1018, 1282, 1394, 1463, 1469, 1486, 1575, 1619). A miss that retrieves them is not necessarily a retrieval failure, and recall for this question is a strong under-count. Six expected ids also make recall@3 impossible, so the capped recall matters.

questions.question: Why are purchase orders waiting for weeks for sign-off?
questions.rationale: Five tickets with different PO numbers and two title forms. Unlabelled competitors: OPS-1788 / OPS-1792 (PO-186850 stuck in approval, a near-duplicate pair outside the cluster).

questions.question: Someone reported the whole system being sluggish.
questions.rationale: A deliberately vague ticket, asked in different words than its text ('Everything is slow today.'). Hard: many infrastructure tickets mention slowness.

questions.question: Which ticket says the AC is not working in the office?
questions.source: vague_ticket_ids: OPS-1632 'AC not working' / 'AC problem in office.'
questions.rationale: DELIBERATE VERBATIM CONTROL: the question repeats the ticket text on purpose, to show that retrieval finds a vague ticket when the wording matches. Competes with the five specific cooling tickets.

questions.question: A customer is asking where their order is and needs help.
questions.source: vague_ticket_ids: OPS-1519 'Where is my order' / 'Customer asking about order. Need help.'
questions.rationale: Vague ticket whose text is a one-line request; competes with tracking and misrouted-shipment tickets.

questions.question: Which tickets report that portal-web-prod-02 is almost out of disk space?
questions.rationale: A near-duplicate pair worded 'Log volume nearly full' and 'Disk usage at 98%'. Both should be retrieved.

questions.question: Was the housekeeping at HQ floor 4 skipped?
questions.rationale: Pair worded 'Cleaning not done at HQ floor 4' and 'Housekeeping contractor missed HQ floor 4'. CL-20 (housekeeping at the HQ server room) is a competing cluster.

questions.question: Why can nobody use the elevator at head office?
questions.rationale: Pair worded 'HQ lift not working' and 'Lift out of service at HQ'. The question uses 'elevator' and 'head office', words that neither title contains.

questions.question: Has the refund to Meridian Retail been paid yet?
questions.rationale: Pair on one pending refund. Meridian Retail also appears in the VPN cluster, so a competing customer name is present.

questions.question: Why did the VPN gateway stop accepting connections?
questions.source: CL-26 members whose category is Infrastructure
questions.rationale: Category filter removes the three Customer Escalation tickets. Every hit must also be Infrastructure.

questions.question: Cooling failure in the server room
questions.source: CL-22 members whose priority is P3-Medium
questions.rationale: Priority filter leaves one of the five cluster tickets. Other P3 cooling tickets outside the cluster may exist (expected is a lower bound).

questions.question: Outbound dispatch halted at Chennai after a power outage
questions.source: CL-27 members whose team is Warehouse Ops
questions.rationale: Team filter splits the cross-category cluster; Facilities tickets must not appear.

questions.question: Temperature excursion or cold chain alarm at Bengaluru
questions.source: CL-13 members created on or after 2025-12-27
questions.rationale: Date filter leaves two of the four cluster tickets (the other two were created 2025-12-12 and 2025-12-26).

questions.question: Which vendor has the most delayed delivery tickets?
questions.source: titles 'Lotus Stretch Wrap delivery late against PO-...' (3 tickets); NorthStar Components and Apex Packaging Ltd have one each
questions.rationale: Aggregation: the answer needs counting across the whole data set, retrieval returns a handful. Measured, not expected to pass.

questions.question: How many tickets are there about cooling failures in the Bengaluru server room?
questions.rationale: A counting question: an honest answer needs all five in the context, which at k=3 is impossible.

questions.question: Who could not log in to the HQ server room?
questions.source: tickets titled 'cannot badge in' / 'Badge access failing' at the HQ server room
questions.rationale: Vocabulary mismatch: the question says 'log in', the tickets say 'badge in'. 29 other tickets use 'log in'.

questions.question: What problems have we had with NorthStar Components?
questions.author: question drafted by the assistant and adopted unchanged by the repository owner; expected ids drafted by the assistant from ticket text and generator metadata after reading the data, so not blind; confirmed by the owner
questions.source: rule: NorthStar Components named in title or description (12 tickets, found by text search)
questions.rationale: Vendor-named question with many true matches (onboarding blocked, late delivery, SLA breach, price mismatch, contract renewal, no ASN). Rule for expected: 'NorthStar Components named in title or description'. Unlabelled competitors: CL-06 OPS-1709, 1756, 1766 name the vendor only in the resolution text ('A pallet delivery from NorthStar Components was missed'). With 12 expected ids recall@3 cannot exceed 0.25 and recall@10 cannot exceed 0.83, so the capped recall matters.

questions.question: Why were the stock counts at Hyderabad so far off?
questions.author: question drafted by the assistant and adopted unchanged by the repository owner; expected ids drafted by the assistant from ticket text and generator metadata after reading the data, so not blind; confirmed by the owner
questions.source: CL-03 (INV-05); the question is read as cycle counts
questions.rationale: Read as cycle counts: CL-03 'Cycle count variance of N% in a zone at Hyderabad'. also_relevant: OPS-1316, 1414, 1784 have the same title form and site but are not in the cluster. The other possible reading is on-hand quantities: CL-30 (WMS sync double-applied adjustments, six tickets) is listed as an unlabelled competitor together with 'cannot find stock' (1150, 1280, 1626, 1628), 'negative on-hand' (1188, 1653) and inventory sync failures (1331, 1480).

questions.question: Which customers complained about late or repeated delivery problems?
questions.author: question drafted by the assistant and adopted unchanged by the repository owner; expected ids drafted by the assistant from ticket text and generator metadata after reading the data, so not blind; confirmed by the owner
questions.source: CL-10 (CE-04), created 2026-05-17 to 2026-06-20, inside the date window
questions.rationale: Date filter 2026-05-01 to 2026-06-30 keeps 143 of 800 tickets; every hit must be inside it. also_relevant: OPS-1399, 1462, 1530 use the same text ('complained for the third time about late and damaged deliveries') but are not in the cluster. Competitors: SLA credit for missed delivery windows (1446, 1493, arguably relevant), tracking not updating (1404, 1497, 1524, weak), damaged-goods claims (1447, 1454, not about lateness).

questions.question: anyone know why coastal beverages keeps asking for sla credits??
questions.author: question drafted by the assistant and adopted unchanged by the repository owner; expected ids drafted by the assistant from ticket text and generator metadata after reading the data, so not blind; confirmed by the owner
questions.rationale: Lowercase customer name, slang and '??' on purpose. also_relevant: OPS-1578 has the same title as 1678 and 1684 ('SLA credit claim from Coastal Beverages') but is not in the cluster. Competitors: SLA-credit tickets of other customers (1068, 1095, 1122, 1284, 1446, 1493, 1710, wrong customer) and other Coastal Beverages tickets about different things (onboarding escalations 1254, 1257, 1410, 1491; billing dispute 1584).

questions.question: Which incidents were caused by something expiring?
questions.author: question drafted by the assistant and adopted unchanged by the repository owner; expected ids drafted by the assistant from ticket text and generator metadata after reading the data, so not blind; confirmed by the owner
questions.source: CL-16 (expired certificate), CL-29 (expired SSO certificate), CL-04 (expired API token)
questions.rationale: Expected is all 14 generator ids. OPS-1552 (CL-04) is Open with no resolution and its text never mentions expiry, so retrieval cannot find the cause there; it is kept so that labels are not adjusted to the scores. Recall is a strong under-count: 32 unlabelled tickets about something expiring exist (8 other certificate expiries, 8 expired password-reset links, 8 contracts expiring next month, 8 near-expiry stock batches). The last two groups are weaker matches (no incident caused by the expiry).
